title: HEARTLAND Protocol App — Clinical Implementation Companion for Rural Heart Failure
description: Progressive Web Application translating the HEARTLAND Protocol (Heart failure Evidence-based Access in Rural Treatment, Linking Advanced Network Delivery) into inspectable implementation-support workflows for rural and resource-limited United States settings. Version 1.9.0 expands the public synthetic sandbox with bounded English- and Spanish-language daily and titration check-ins; optional voice interaction; simulated outreach and morning-round automation; a provider Copilot over 13 read-only deterministic tools; five-day synthetic scenarios; deterministic population replay for 500, 2,500, or 5,000 fictional check-ins; a Chart-to-Call-to-Document review workflow; protocol-grounded explanations; human-controlled SBAR wording proposals; Evidence Flow; and Decision Receipts. The language-model layer converses, extracts, explains, summarizes, and drafts. Version-controlled protocol-derived rules and explicit missing-data policies set simulated dispositions, and a human reviewer authorizes any next action. Deterministic preflight checks, bounded output screening, atomic usage limits, and graceful fallbacks constrain the public demonstration. Built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Supabase. The public sandbox uses synthetic data. This release demonstrates implemented and inspectable software; it does not establish clinical validation, institutional deployment, regulatory status, adoption, clinical safety, efficacy, staffing effects, or patient outcomes.
notes: Release boundary: the public sandbox uses synthetic data and is intended for technical demonstration and controlled evaluation. Real PHI and unsupervised clinical use are not authorized. The September 1, 2026 release snapshot passed 1,355 unit and integration tests, 72 desktop/mobile end-to-end tests, and 44 database authorization contracts, together with lint, typecheck, production build, security scan, npm audit at the high threshold, CodeQL, and CycloneDX SBOM generation. These are software-quality controls, not clinical validation. The selected emergency-language and obvious-identifier screens are bounded safeguards, not comprehensive detection or de-identification. Institution-specific clinical, privacy, security, regulatory, accessibility, and workflow evaluation remain required before any governed real-world deployment. The HEARTLAND Risk Stratification Framework remains proposed and unvalidated against clinical outcomes data.
